'''Toney Bernard Douglas''' (born March 16, 1986) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Hapoel Galil Elyon]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].

He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]], and the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. Douglas was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]] with the 29th overall pick, but was immediately traded to the [[New York Knicks]]. He played for the Knicks, [[Houston Rockets]], [[Sacramento Kings]] and the [[Golden State Warriors]] before being traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in 2014. After spending the 2014–15 season in China with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]], he returned to the NBA in 2015, joining the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].

He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]] for one year, eventually becoming frustrated with his role on the team as a [[shooting guard]]. He subsequently transferred to the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]] for the remainder of his collegiate career, switching to the [[point guard]] position. Emerging as a defensive force in his junior season, Douglas set school and conference records for [[steal (basketball)|steal]]s. He stepped up as a team leader in his final season, breaking personal records in several statistical categories and helped lead the Seminoles to their first [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]] in 11 years.

==Early life==
Douglas was born to Harry and Stephanie Douglas in [[Tampa, Florida]], but moved to [[Jonesboro, Georgia]] with his parents as a youth. He attended [[Jonesboro High School (Georgia)|Jonesboro High School]], where he was starter for its basketball team for three years. Douglas played alongside his brother, [[Harry Douglas|Harry]], for the same amount of time. He spent most of his [[freshman#United States|freshman]] season (2000–01) on the [[junior varsity team]].<ref name="AJC-Auburn">{{cite news|title=Jonesboro Taps Star's Powers \ Bound For Auburn|last=Bricks|first=Peter|date=January 8, 2004|work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|publisher=InfoTrac|page=J15}}</ref> In the 2001–02 season, when he was made a starter,<ref name="AJC-Auburn" /> Douglas averaged 21.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game, and became the first sophomore to earn first-team honors at the all-region and all-state levels. In his junior season, Douglas averaged 28.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game, scoring 20 points or more 24 times. He was named the Georgia Class 5A Player of the Year, and helped lead the team to the championship game of the state playoffs.

Douglas averaged 34 points per game as a senior, and the team advanced as far as the state semifinals. He departed Jonesboro High as [[Clayton County, Georgia|Clayton County]]'s leading scorer, with 2,404 points. He was subsequently named fourth-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] and earned a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] nomination.<ref name="Bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.seminoles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/douglas_toney00.html|title=Player Bio: Toney Douglas|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=August 7, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727033728/http://www.seminoles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/douglas_toney00.html|archive-date=July 27, 2011}}</ref> Considered a [[four-star recruit]] by [[Rivals.com]], Douglas was listed as the No. 14 shooting guard and the No. 66 player in the nation in 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Toney-Douglas-12211|title=Toney Douglas Recruiting Profile|work=Rivals.com|access-date=July 11, 2012}}</ref>

==College career==

===Auburn===
Douglas committed to [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn University]] during his junior year of high school.<ref name="AJC-Auburn" /> Playing as the starting [[shooting guard]] in his freshman season (2004–05), he led the team in scoring at 16.9 points per game (5th in the SEC), with a .424 [[field goal percentage]] (10th in the SEC) and .789 [[free throw percentage]] (7th), and scored a team season-high (as well as career high) 38 points against [[Nicholls State Colonels men's basketball|Nicholls State]].<ref name=sportsref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/toney-douglas-1.html?_gl=1*1wyp3g7*_ga*MTg4NzA1MTAwMi4xNzgxOTM0NTkz*_ga_80FRT7VJ60*czE3ODI2MTUzNzEkbzExJGcxJHQxNzgyNjE3MDg4JGo2MCRsMCRoMA.. "Toney Douglas,"] sports-reference.com.</ref><ref name="Bio" /><ref name="Transfer">{{cite news|title=Auburn star transferring to FSU; Douglas, SEC fifth-leading scorer, will play for Seminoles in 2006–07|last=Schoffel|first=Ira|date=June 30, 2005|work=The Florida Times-Union|publisher=InfoTrac|page=C-8}}</ref> Douglas, who had the second-highest freshman scoring average in the nation, was voted to the All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) Freshman Team, third-team Freshman All-America, and third-team All-SEC—he was the fourth Auburn freshman to be named to the latter.<ref name="Bio" />

===Transfer===
Douglas submitted his name for the [[NBA draft]] in the 2005 offseason, but did not sign with an [[sports agent|agent]], which allowed  him to remain eligible for college when he later withdrew from the process.<ref name="Transfer" /><ref name="Release">{{cite news|title=Auburn Grants Douglas Release|date=June 15, 2005|work=The Cincinnati Post|publisher=InfoTrac|page=B2}}</ref> Despite Douglas' success at Auburn, he and his family were unhappy with his position on the basketball team. Douglas wanted to be the team's [[point guard]], which he believed was his more natural position and the one he would play in the [[NBA]]. However, team management did not accede to his request, prompting him to request a transfer. Then-coach [[Jeff Lebo]] granted Douglas his scholarship release on the condition that he transfer to a non-SEC university.

===Florida State===

On June 29, 2005, Douglas enrolled at [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State University]], where coach [[Leonard Hamilton]] allowed him to play point guard.<ref name="SPT-sparkplug">{{cite news|title=Spectator now sparkplug for 'Noles|last=Landman|first=Brian|date=December 3, 2006|work=The St. Petersburg Times|publisher=InfoTrac|page=3C}}</ref> Because [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) rules stipulate that players who transfer must sit out the following season, Douglas only began playing with the team in the 2006–07 season, though he practiced with them during 2005–06.<ref name="Bio" /><ref name="Transfer" /><ref name="Release" />

====Sophomore year====
Douglas initially struggled at the point guard position while adjusting to the Florida State offense, but continued to play well in other respects. The early part of his sophomore season was highlighted by his shot block that helped to seal an upset victory against the then-fourth-ranked [[Florida Gators men's basketball|University of Florida Gators]], and a late-game period against [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] in which he scored 10 consecutive points, leading Florida State to a win.<ref name="GatorsDefeat">{{cite news|title=Block helps Seminoles stun Gators|last=Landman|first=Brian|date=December 4, 2006|work=The St. Petersburg Times|publisher=InfoTrac|page=1C}}</ref><ref name="FTU-adjustment">{{cite news|title=Playing near home drives FSU's Douglas; Transfer, still adjusting to a new position, excited about trip to play Georgia Tech|last=Thomas|first=Bob|date=January 12, 2007|work=The Florida Times-Union|publisher=InfoTrac|page=C-1}}</ref><ref name="Deacons-victory">{{cite news|title=Douglas Steps Up At The Right Time|last=Carter|first=Scott|date=January 28, 2007|work=The Tampa Tribune|publisher=InfoTrac|page=12}}</ref> On February 7, 2007, Douglas injured the fourth [[metacarpal]] in his right  (shooting) hand, forcing him to sit out six games (nearly a month)—of which Florida State lost five.<ref name="Hand injury">{{cite news|title=Douglas out, 'Noles turning to Mims|last=Landman|first=Brian|date=February 10, 2007|work=The St. Petersburg Times|publisher=InfoTrac|page=6C}}</ref><ref name="Injury return">{{cite news|title=Douglas' sharp return helps boost outlook|last=Landman|first=Brian|date=March 4, 2007|work=The St. Petersburg Times|publisher=InfoTrac|page=11C}}</ref>

In his first game (against the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|University of Miami]]) after sustaining his injury, Douglas scored 13 points, including a [[three-point field goal|three-pointer]] that tied the game and forced [[Overtime (sports)#Basketball|overtime]]; Florida State went on to win the game.<ref name="Injury return" /> Douglas finished the season with averages of 12.7 points, 2.9 assists, and 2.7 rebounds per game.<ref name="Bio" /> In three games of the [[2007 National Invitation Tournament]] (NIT), he averaged 11.7 points and 3.7 rebounds, as Florida State won twice before losing to [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State University]] in the semifinals.<ref name="Bio" /><ref name="2007-NIT">{{cite news|title=Douglas, Swann Lead Seminoles in a Rout|date=March 16, 2007|work=The Cincinnati Post|publisher=InfoTrac|page=B6}}</ref>

====Junior year====
[[File:Toney Douglas 2007.jpg|thumb|left|Douglas in 2007]]
In his junior season, Douglas continued his transition to point guard, creating offensive opportunities for others on the team in addition to scoring by himself. Although he still needed to work on polishing the distribution aspect of his game, coach Hamilton said in January 2008 that "he's done an exceptional job when you take into consideration this hasn't been his role prior to coming to Florida State."<ref name="Point-transition">{{cite news|title=Douglas' play on point; The ex-shooting guard has done well developing into FSU's floor leader|last=Thomas|first=Bob|date=January 26, 2008|work=The Florida Times-Union|publisher=InfoTrac|page=C-6}}</ref> Douglas' defense improved considerably; he accumulated 2.6 steals per game (7th in the SEC) as a junior (compared to 1.2 steals in the previous season), the highest rate in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]]. <ref name=sportsref/> His total of 48 steals in 16 games against [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] teams was the third-highest in league history. He averaged 15.4 points per game (9th), with an .809 free throw percentage  (8th). <ref name=sportsref/>  In a game against the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|University of Virginia]], Douglas' steal in the final minute (his sixth of the game) and subsequent [[free throw]]s carried Florida State to a win that helped their chances of being selected to the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2008 NCAA tournament]].<ref name="Bio" /><ref>{{cite news|title=Stop on Cavs Star Clinches W for FSU|last=Givens|first=Jamey|date=January 24, 2008|work=The St. Petersburg Times|publisher=InfoTrac|page=4C}}</ref>

After the regular season concluded, Douglas was selected into the ACC All-Defensive Team and the All-ACC Third Team.<ref name="ACC awards 2008">{{cite web|url=http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031008aab.html|title=Atlantic Coast Sports Media Association Announces the 2007–08 All-ACC Men's Basketball Teams|date=March 10, 2008|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference (CBS Interactive)|access-date=August 10, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121209011946/http://www.theacc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031008aab.html|archive-date=December 9, 2012}}</ref> Despite Douglas' efforts (18 points, 5 assists, and 3 steals) against [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] in the quarterfinals, Florida State lost the game, effectively shutting them out from the NCAA tournament.<ref name="Bio" /><ref name="2008_ACCQuarters">{{cite news|title=College Basketball: ACC Tournament: Focus on Georgians |last=Winkeljohn|first=Matt|date=March 15, 2008|work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|publisher=InfoTrac|page=D5}}</ref> After Florida State lost in the first round of the [[2008 NIT]], Douglas finished the season with 90 steals, second only to [[Sam Cassell]] in the number of steals made in one season (97).<ref name="2008_ACCQuarters" /><ref name="2008-NIT">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=280780052|title=Akron Zips vs. Florida State Seminoles – Box Score|date=March 18, 2008|publisher=ESPN|access-date=August 10, 2009}}</ref> He led the team in scoring (15.4 ppg), steals (2.6 spg; also highest in the ACC), and assists (2.6).<ref name="Bio" />

====Senior year====
The 2008–09 Florida State team was composed of mostly freshman and sophomores, which meant that the veteran Douglas, now a senior (one of three on the team),<ref name="Winston-Clemson">{{cite news|title=Duke has had recent success at FSU N.C. State will also open conference play, traveling to play unbeaten Clemson|last=Cole|first=Bill|date=January 10, 2009|work=Winston-Salem Journal|publisher=InfoTrac|page=C1}}</ref> featured more prominently in the offense than in previous years. He started all 35 games of the season, one of two Seminole players to do so. Douglas became the primary threat on offense, and was the sole top scorer for the team in 23 games. His scoring average increased by more than six points, to 21.5 points per game, which was the highest average on the team and in the ACC as he led the ACC as well with 751 total points; he also averaged 2.9 assists, a team and career high, 1.8 steals (5th), and 3.9 rebounds, as well as an .810 free throw percentage (10th(.<ref name=sportsref/><ref name="Bio" /><ref name="NBA-draftprofile">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/draft2009/prospects/133.html|title=Toney Douglas – Prospect Profile|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=August 13, 2009}}</ref> He earned ACC All-Defensive Team honors again and was selected to the All-ACC First Team.<ref name="Bio" /> His other major honors included being named the ACC Defensive Player of the Year, receiving the second-most votes for ACC Player of the Year and his selection to the [[Associated Press]]' All-America Third Team.<ref name="SN-ACCDPOY">{{cite news|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/college-basketball/article/2009-03-10/fsus-douglas-named-acc-defensive-player-year|title=FSU's Douglas named ACC defensive player of year|date=March 10, 2009|work=Sporting News|access-date=August 12, 2009}}{{Dead link|date=March 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name="ESPN-APallamerica">{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=4027698|title=Griffin, Hansbrough lead AP first team|date=March 31, 2009|publisher=ESPN|access-date=August 12, 2009}}</ref>

Douglas' strong play in the ACC tournament, in which the Seminoles upset top-ranked North Carolina and advanced to their first ACC final, led to his selection to the ACC All-Tournament team, another first for a Florida State player.<ref name="ACCTourn09">{{cite news|title=FSU Loss has Silver Lining; 'Noles fall in ACC tourney final but still have NCAA berth|last=Landman|first=Brian|date=March 16, 2009|work=The St. Petersburg Times|publisher=InfoTrac|page=1X}}</ref> The Seminoles made their first appearance in the NCAA tournament in 11 years, playing against the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|University of Wisconsin]]. Douglas played well, scoring 26 points, but he missed an important three-point attempt late in the game and had [[Trévon Hughes]] score the winning shot while defending him. Wisconsin won 61–59 in overtime, thus ending Douglas' collegiate career.<ref name="NCAA-loss">{{cite news|title=Uw Holds Douglas in Check the Florida State Star Scores 26 Points, but the Badgers Harass Him into a Key Miss down the Stretch|last=Schultz|first=Rob|date=March 21, 2009|work=The Capital Times|access-date=August 12, 2009|url=http://find.galegroup.com.lsproxy.austincc.edu/gtx/retrieve.do?contentSet=IAC-Documents&resultListType=RESULT_LIST&qrySerId=Locale%28en%2C%2C%29%3AFQE%3D%28KE%2CNone%2C13%29Toney+Douglas%24&sgHitCountType=None&inPS=true&sort=DateDescend&searchType=BasicSearchForm&tabID=T004&prodId=SPN.SP00&searchId=R7&currentPosition=13&userGroupName=txshracd2487&docId=CJ196132183&docType=IAC|url-access=registration}}{{Dead link|date=March 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===New York Knicks (2009–2012)===
In preparation for the [[2009 NBA draft]], Douglas worked out at the [[NBA draft combine]] during May 28–29, and participated in pre-draft workouts with ten teams.<ref name="Combine">{{cite news|url=http://infoweb.newsbank.com/iw-search/we/InfoWeb?p_action=doc&p_topdoc=1&p_docnum=1&p_sort=YMD_date:D&p_product=NewsBank&p_text_direct-0=document_id=%28%201283B379D6FCA8A8%20%29&p_docid=1283B379D6FCA8A8&p_theme=aggregated5&p_queryname=1283B379D6FCA8A8&f_openurl=yes&p_nbid=M59W4FJGMTI1MDYyMzA0MC45NTU3MzI6MTo3OnJmLTg3MjU&&p_multi=ORLB|title=NBA combine taps Calathes, Taylor|last=Deitch|first=Dennis|date=June 6, 2009|work=The Orlando Sentinel|publisher=NewsBank|url-access=registration |page=C2|access-date=August 17, 2009}}</ref><ref name="Workouts">{{cite news|url=http://infoweb.newsbank.com/iw-search/we/InfoWeb?p_action=doc&p_topdoc=1&p_docnum=1&p_sort=YMD_date:D&p_product=NewsBank&p_text_direct-0=document_id=%28%201290392C4359B250%20%29&p_docid=1290392C4359B250&p_theme=aggregated5&p_queryname=1290392C4359B250&f_openurl=yes&p_nbid=V5DQ53RKMTI1MDYyMjk0My43MTk4MzM6MTo3OnJmLTg3MjU&&p_multi=ORLB|title=Douglas waits anxiously|last=Carter|first=Andrew|date=June 23, 2009|work=The Orlando Sentinel|publisher=NewsBank|url-access=registration |page=C1|access-date=August 17, 2009}}</ref>

On June 25, 2009, Douglas was selected by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] with the 29th overall pick in the 2009 NBA draft, making him the first Seminole guard to be drafted in the first round since [[Bob Sura]] (1995).<ref name="TalDem-NBASL09">{{cite news|url=http://www.tallahassee.com/article/20090721/FSU05/907210318/1008/FSU |title=Ex-'Noles guards convene in Vegas at NBA Summer League |last=Tomasson |first=Chris |date=July 21, 2009 |work=Tallahassee Democrat |access-date=August 15, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230153227/http://www.tallahassee.com/article/20090721/FSU05/907210318/1008/FSU |archive-date=December 30, 2014 }}</ref> Later that night, the [[New York Knicks]] acquired the rights to Douglas in exchange for a second-round draft pick in 2011 and $3 million in cash considerations.<ref name="PalmBeachPost"/><ref name="LakersToKnicks">{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4285133|title=Knicks acquire 29th pick from Lakers|date=June 25, 2009|publisher=ESPN|access-date=August 13, 2009}}</ref> He signed with the Knicks on July 9, 2009<ref name="Signed">{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4317065|title=Douglas expected in summer league|date=July 9, 2009|publisher=ESPN|access-date=August 13, 2009}}</ref> and averaged a team-high 7.0 assists per game during the [[NBA Summer League]].<ref name="SummerLeague2009">{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks_summerleague09.html|title=2009 Knicks Summer League Central|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=August 13, 2009}}</ref>

During the [[2009–10 NBA season|2009–10 season]], Douglas was a reserve guard, and averaged 8.6 points, 2.0 assists, and 0.8 steals per game, while shooting .458 from the field and .809 from the free throw line.<ref name=sportsref/>

In 2010-11, he averaged 10.6 points, 3.0 assists, and 1.1 steals per game.<ref name=sportsref/> He scored a career-high 30 points in a win against the [[Chicago Bulls]] on November 4, 2010.<ref name="NBACareerHigh">{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=301104004|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716002459/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=301104004|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 16, 2012|title=Toney Douglas, Danilo Gallinari lead Knicks' offense in win over Bulls|date=November 4, 2010|publisher=ESPN|access-date=November 5, 2010}}</ref> On March 17, 2011, Douglas tied a Knicks record with nine three-pointers in a home win against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].

In 2011-12 he saw less time on the court, and averaged 6.2 points, 2.0 assists, and 0.8 steals per game, while shooting .846 from the free throw line.<ref name=sportsref/>

===Houston Rockets (2012–2013)===
[[File:Toney Douglas.jpg|thumb|right|Douglas with the Houston Rockets in 2012]]
On July 11, 2012, Douglas was traded, along with [[Josh Harrellson]], [[Jerome Jordan]], two future second-round draft picks and cash considerations, to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Marcus Camby]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-make-trades-official|title=Rockets Make Trades Official|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2012|access-date=July 11, 2012}}</ref> His best game as a Rocket came on December 4, 2012, when he scored a season-high 22 points against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/douglto01/gamelog/2013/|title=Toney Douglas 2012–13 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 3, 2016}}</ref> In 2012-13 with the team he averaged 7.5 points, 2.1 assists, and 1.0 steals per game, while shooting  .882 from the free throw line.<ref name=sportsref/>

===Sacramento Kings (2013)===
On February 20, 2013, Douglas was traded, along with [[Cole Aldrich]] and [[Patrick Patterson (basketball)|Patrick Patterson]], to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Thomas Robinson (basketball)|Thomas Robinson]], [[Francisco García (basketball)|Francisco García]] and [[Tyler Honeycutt]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-complete-multiplayer-trade | title=Kings Complete Multiplayer Trade | work=NBA.com | date=February 20, 2013 | access-date=February 21, 2013}}</ref> In 2013 with the team he averaged 6.1 points, 2.6  assists, and 1.4 steals per game, while sinking all of his foul shots.<ref name=sportsref/>

===Golden State Warriors (2013–2014)===
On July 18, 2013, Douglas signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/douglas-signing-071813|title=Warriors Sign Free Agent Guard Toney Douglas to Contract|work=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2013|access-date=July 18, 2013}}</ref> He made 24 appearances for the franchise, averaging 11 minutes per game in a limited bench role. Throughout his brief tenure, he struggled with his accuracy, shooting only 37.2% from the field.

===Miami Heat (2014)===
On January 15, 2014, Douglas was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in a three-team deal involving the Warriors and the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-trade-joel-anthony-exchange-toney-douglas|title=HEAT Trade Joel Anthony in Exchange for Toney Douglas|work=NBA.com|date=January 15, 2014|access-date=January 15, 2014}}</ref> The Heat made their fourth straight appearance in the NBA Finals in [[2014 NBA Finals|2014]], but lost the series in five games to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].

===China (2014–2015)===
On August 19, 2014, Douglas signed a one-year deal with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/131901/toney-douglas-signs-with-jiangsu-dragons.html|title=Toney Douglas signs with Jiangsu Dragons|work=Sportando.com|date=August 19, 2014|access-date=August 19, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oneworldsports.com/blogs/jiangsu-signs-former-nbaer-toney-douglas|title=JIANGSU GETS FORMER NBA MAN TONEY DOUGLAS|work=OneWorldSports.com|date=August 19, 2014|access-date=August 19, 2014|archive-date=October 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005092532/http://www.oneworldsports.com/blogs/jiangsu-signs-former-nbaer-toney-douglas|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 1, 2015, he terminated his contract with Jiangsu following the conclusion of the regular season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/150756/the-complete-list-of-players-available-from-china.html|title=The complete list of players available from China|work=Sportando.com|date=February 1, 2015|access-date=February 1, 2015}}</ref> He appeared in 35 games while averaging 24.9 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.3 assists, and 2.1 steals (7th in the league) per game.<ref name=real>[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Toney-Douglas/Summary/1624 "Toney Douglas,"] basketball.realgm.com.</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2015–2016)===
On February 4, 2015, Douglas signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-toney-douglas-10-day-contract|title=Pelicans Sign Toney Douglas to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 4, 2014|access-date=February 4, 2014}}</ref> On February 18, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pelicans Sign Toney Douglas to Second 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-toney-douglas-second-10-day-contract|access-date=February 18, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=February 18, 2015}}</ref> However, the next day, he was waived by the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-toney-douglas|title=Pelicans Waive Toney Douglas|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 19, 2015}}</ref> He returned to the Pelicans on March 24, signing with the team for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-re-sign-toney-douglas|title=Pelicans Re-Sign Toney Douglas|work=NBA.com|date=March 24, 2015|access-date=July 31, 2015}}</ref> On July 31, he was waived again by the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-guard-toney-douglas|title=Pelicans Waive Toney Douglas|work=NBA.com|date=July 31, 2015|access-date=July 31, 2015}}</ref> In 2015-16 with the team he averaged 8.7 points, 2.6 assists, and 1.1 steals per game, while shooting  .848 from the free throw line.<ref name=sportsref/>

On August 11, 2015, Douglas signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/pacers-sign-free-agent-toney-douglas|title=Pacers Sign Free Agent Toney Douglas|date=August 11, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=August 11, 2015}}</ref> However, he was waived by the Pacers on October 26 after appearing in five preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/pacers-waive-toney-douglas|title=Pacers Waive Toney Douglas|date=October 26, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 26, 2015}}</ref> Four days later, he re-signed with the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-toney-douglas|title=Pelicans Sign Toney Douglas|date=October 30, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 30, 2015}}</ref> On March 31, 2016, he recorded 20 points and a season-high 10 assists in a 101–95 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160331/DENNOP/gameinfo.html|title=Babbitt leads Pelicans past Nuggets 101–95|date=March 31, 2016|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 1, 2016}}</ref> On July 12, 2016, he was waived by the Pelicans.<ref>{{cite web|last=Reid|first=John|url=http://www.nola.com/pelicans/index.ssf/2016/07/pelicans_waive_point_guard_ton.html|title=Pelicans waive point guard Toney Douglas to avoid extending guaranteed contract|date=July 12, 2016|work=NOLA.com|access-date=July 13, 2016}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2016–2017)===
On October 3, 2016, Douglas signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/douglas-signing-161003|title=Cavaliers Sign Point Guard Toney Douglas|work=NBA.com|date=October 3, 2016|access-date=October 3, 2016}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Cavaliers on October 15 after appearing in five preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/smith-signing-2016|title=Cavaliers Re-Sign Guard J.R. Smith|work=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2016|access-date=October 15, 2016}}</ref> On December 5, 2016, he signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] to help the team deal with numerous injuries. Memphis had to use an NBA hardship exemption in order to sign him as he made their roster stand at 16, one over the allowed limited of 15.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/douglas-signed-161205|title=Grizzlies sign Toney Douglas|work=NBA.com|date=December 5, 2016|access-date=December 5, 2016}}</ref> He appeared in six games for the Grizzlies before he was waived by the team on December 15.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/toney-douglas-waived-161215|title=Grizzlies waive Toney Douglas|work=NBA.com|date=December 15, 2016|access-date=December 15, 2016}}</ref> On January 30, 2017, he signed a 10-day contract with the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/toney-douglas-re-signed-170130|title=Grizzlies re-sign Toney Douglas to 10-day contract|work=NBA.com|date=January 30, 2017|access-date=January 30, 2017}}</ref> He went on to sign a second 10-day contract with the Grizzlies on February 9,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/toney-douglas-signed-to-second-10-day-170209|title=Grizzlies sign Toney Douglas to second 10-day contract|work=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2017|access-date=February 9, 2017}}</ref> and then a rest-of-season contract on February 23.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/douglas-sign-for-the-remainder-of-season-170223|title=Grizzlies sign Toney Douglas for the remainder of the 2016–17 season|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017}}</ref> On March 18, 2017, Douglas was again waived by the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/wayne-selden-signed-douglas-waived-170318|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Wayne Selden Jr.|work=NBA.com|date=March 18, 2017|access-date=March 18, 2017}}</ref>

===Turkey (2017–2019)===

====Anadolu Efes (2017–2018)====
On December 29, 2017, Douglas signed with Turkish club [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] for the rest of the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Efes adds Toney Douglas until end of season|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8fklhtv95tumnom4/efes-adds-toney-douglas-until-end-of-season|access-date=December 29, 2017|work=EuroLeague.net|date=December 29, 2017}}</ref> Douglas helped Anadolu Efes to win the [[2018 Turkish Basketball Cup|2018 Turkish Cup]] . In 2017-18 with the team he averaged 8.8 points, 2.1 assists, and 0.4 steals per game, while shooting .852 from the free throw line.<ref name=real/>

====Sakarya (2018)====
On August 6, 2018, Douglas signed with [[Sakarya BB]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{cite web|title=Toney Douglas signed with Sakarya|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/722717/toney-douglas-signed-with-sakarya/|work=EuroHoops.net|date=August 6, 2018|access-date=December 5, 2018}}</ref> In 15 games played for Sakarya, Douglas averaged 15.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 6.6 assists and 2.3 steals per game.

====Darüşşafaka (2018–2019)====
On December 5, 2018, Douglas parted ways with Sakarya and signed with [[Darüşşafaka S.K.|Darüşşafaka]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Darussafaka adds guard Douglas|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9ayubya3tagf49q8|work=EuroLeague.net|date=December 5, 2018|access-date=December 5, 2018}}</ref>

===Spain & Italy (2019–2021)===
On November 26, 2019, Douglas signed with [[CB Estudiantes|Movistar Estudiantes]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/toney-douglas-signs-with-estudiantes/|title=Toney Douglas signs with Estudiantes|date=November 26, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=November 26, 2019|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref> On February 21, 2020, after he played in 11 games, he and the team parted ways.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://piratasdelbasket.net/toney-douglas-abandonara-el-movistar-estudiantes/|title=Toney Douglas abandonará el Movistar Estudiantes|date=February 21, 2020|publisher=piratasdelbasket.net|language=es|access-date=February 25, 2020}}</ref><ref name=real/>

On March 2, 2020, Douglas signed with [[Pallacanestro Varese|Varese]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{cite web |title=TONEY DOUGLAS È UN NUOVO GIOCATORE DELLA OPENJOBMETIS |url=http://www.pallacanestrovarese.it/toney-douglas-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-della-openjobmetis/ |publisher=pallacanestrovarese.it |date=2 March 2019 |language=it |access-date=March 2, 2020 |archive-date=October 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020192141/https://www.pallacanestrovarese.it/toney-douglas-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-della-openjobmetis/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In that period the Italian team was looking to replace [[Jason Clark (basketball)|Jason Clark]] who quit before the end of the season. In 26 games during the 2020–2021 season, Douglas averaged 14.7 points, 4.3 rebounds, 4.9 assists, and 1.2 steals per contest.<ref name=real/>

===Greece (2021–2022)===
On August 21, 2021, Douglas signed with Greek club [[G.S. Iraklis B.C.|Iraklis Thessaloniki]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Iraklis lands Toney Douglas |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/iraklis-lands-toney-douglas/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 22, 2021 |date=August 22, 2021|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> In 18 [[Greek Basket League|league]], [[Greek Basketball Cup|cup]], and [[FIBA Europe Cup|European competition]] matches, he averaged 16 points, 5.5 rebounds, 4.5 assists, and 2 steals, playing 32 minutes per contest.

===Israel (2022)===
On January 22, 2022, Douglas signed with Israeli club [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Toney Douglas signs with Hapoel Eilat |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/toney-douglas-signs-with-hapoel-eilat/ |website=Sportando |access-date=January 22, 2022 |date=January 22, 2022|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> In 13 games, Douglas averaged 17.9 points (2nd in the league), 3.5 assists, and 1.7 steals (3rd) per contest, with a .429 three-point percentage (leading the league) and a .500 field goal percentage (5th).<ref name=real/><ref name=sportsref/>

===Benfica (2022–2024)===
On August 14, 2022, Douglas signed with [[S.L. Benfica (basketball)|Benfica]] of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Basquetebol]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/benfica-officially-lands-toney-douglas/|title=Benfica officially lands Toney Douglas|last=|first=|date=August 14, 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 17, 2022|last1=Borghesan |first1=Ennio Terrasi }}</ref>  In 2022-23, in 47 games, Douglas averaged 13.2 points, 3.7 assists, and 1.7 steals per contest, with a .408 three-point percentage.<ref name=real/>

In 2023-24, in 38 games, Douglas averaged 10.1 points, 3.0 assists, and 1.8 steals per contest, with an .808 three-point percentage.<ref name=real/>

===FC Porto (2024–25)===
On August 9, 2024, Douglas signed with [[FC Porto (basketball)|FC Porto]] also of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Basquetebol]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fcporto.pt/pt/noticias/20240809-pt-toney-douglas-e-dragao|title=Toney Douglas is a Dragon|last=|first=|date=August 9, 2024|website=|newspaper=fcporto.pt|language=En|access-date=August 9, 2024|last1=Borghesan |first1=Ennio Terrasi }}</ref> In 2024-25, in 41 games, Douglas averaged 12.6 points, 4.2 assists, and 1.6 steals per contest, with an .840 free throw percentage.<ref name=real/>

===Israel  (2025–present)===
On October 10, 2025,  Douglas signed with [[Bnei Herzliya Basket|Bnei Herzelia]] of the [[Israeli  Basketball Premier League]].<ref name=real/> He played seven games with the team before switching to another Israeli team.<ref name=real/>

Playing for [[Hapoel Galil Elyon]] of the Israeli Basketball Premier League in 2025-26, in 20 games he averaged 7.7 points,  1.6 assists, and 0.6 steals per contest.<ref name=real/>

==Personal life==
Douglas' brother, [[Harry Douglas|Harry]], is a former wide receiver who played ten seasons with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] and [[Tennessee Titans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref name="PalmBeachPost">{{cite news|title=Former 'Nole Douglas goes to Knicks|work=The Palm Beach Post|date=June 26, 2009|publisher=InfoTrac|page=1c}}</ref> In 2009, the Douglases became only the sixth set of brothers to play in the NBA and NFL.<ref name="NBA-NFL_brothers">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/07/20/sports/basketball/20knicks.html|title=Sibling rivalry benefits Knicks' Douglas|last=Abrams|first=Jonathan|date=July 20, 2009|work=The New York Times|access-date=August 7, 2009}}</ref>
